description: A two-panel secondary-electron SEM figure of fracture surfaces, showing typical inclusions sitting inside ductile dimples. (a) is a lower-magnification micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar; the surface is dominated by fine equiaxed dimples (typical of ductile overload) with a cluster of larger, deeper dimples at upper centre containing small rounded/globular second-phase particles. White arrows point to these particles, which are labelled "Mn(Mg)S" in the panel. The matrix between dimples shows tearing ridges. (b) is a higher-magnification micrograph with a 2 µm scale bar showing one large dimple whose interior holds several angular, blocky/faceted particles of roughly a few hundred nanometres to ~1 µm; white arrows point to these particles, labelled "AlN". The elongated dimple walls around them suggest the particles acted as nucleation sites for void formation. Together the panels demonstrate that two distinct inclusion populations — globular Mn(Mg)S in (a) and angular AlN in (b) — are located at dimple bottoms, i.e. they initiated microvoids during ductile fracture. The citation link states that (b) corresponds to aggregated AlN inclusions detected in the HN steel. No numeric values other than the two scale bars are printed.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an SEM fracture surface with a 10 µm scale bar; the surface consists of fine equiaxed dimples with tearing ridges between them.
White arrows in panel (a) point to small globular particles at the bottom of a cluster of deeper dimples, annotated with the label "Mn(Mg)S".
Panel (b) is a higher-magnification SEM image with a 2 µm scale bar showing one large dimple containing angular, faceted particles.
White arrows in panel (b) point to the angular particles, which are annotated "AlN".
The caption states the figure shows typical inclusions located in the dimples of a fracture surface.
The citing text states that aggregated AlN inclusions were detected in the HN steel, referring to Figure 12b.
The citing text states the aggregated AlN inclusions could deteriorate the steel properties.
The citing text attributes aggregated AlN formation to the smelting process via combined effects of the cavity bridge and viscous resistance (citing Wang et al.[22]).
Both labelled inclusion types sit within dimples, i.e. they appear to have acted as microvoid nucleation sites during ductile fracture.
The two inclusion morphologies differ: Mn(Mg)S appears globular/rounded in (a), whereas AlN appears angular and blocky in (b).

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of a ductile fracture surface with a 10 µm scale bar; fine dimples plus a cluster of deeper dimples containing small globular particles indicated by white arrows and labelled "Mn(Mg)S".
Higher-magnification SEM micrograph with a 2 µm scale bar showing a single large dimple containing angular/blocky particles indicated by white arrows and labelled "AlN".
